Verified at 4a14400. The loop follows the /v1/models contract (limit=1000, after_id cursor) and terminates on !has_more, empty last_id, or a repeated cursor.

Proof: the 18 Anthropic tests pass in-tree at this head, including the new pagination test; that same test fails on current main, which returns only the first page, so it discriminates. I also probed the loop guards against a stub server: a stuck cursor (has_more=true with last_id echoing the request) terminates after one extra hop, and has_more=true with an empty last_id terminates immediately.

LGTM.

The truncation is real — the endpoint defaults to 20 items per page and an account's list (with dated snapshots) already sits near that boundary — so the direction is right. Two ways to land it, either is fine:

- **Keep just `limit=1000`.** It is the endpoint maximum, so a single request already returns everything the API can hand back; the loop only earns its keep above that count. One line, no extra requests, and none of the loop's edge cases to reason about.
- **Or keep the loop and bound it.** As written, termination depends on `has_more` turning false or `last_id` repeating, so a server that keeps returning a fresh `last_id` with `has_more: true` still loops forever — the description's "cannot cause an endless loop" only holds for repeated ids. A `for page := 0; page < N; page++` cap (with the existing checks kept) makes that statement true and turns the worst case into N requests instead of unbounded growth.

Either way, please state in the description that 1000 is the accepted maximum: `ListModels` is also what `CheckConnection` uses (`anthropic.go:576`), so a value the API rejects with 400 would turn connection checks into failures.

Respin verified at 66f41bf. The loop is now bounded by anthropicModelsMaxPages (100) with an explicit error past the cap, which makes the "cannot loop forever" claim true even against a server that keeps returning a fresh cursor, and CheckConnection inherits the same bound.

Executed verification at 66f41bf28 (CGO_ENABLED=0): all Anthropic ListModels tests pass, including the new TestAnthropicListModelsStopsOnEndlessCursors, which simulates has_more:true with an ever-fresh last_id and asserts an error after exactly 100 requests - a direct negative control for the cap. Full internal/entity/models package is green (15.4s).

Approving at this head.
Thanks for update, all feedback has been addressed. LGTM.

review_comments.body:
** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Reject pagination cursors that cannot complete the list.** If a provider returns `last_id` values A, B, A while `has_more` remains true, this check never stops the loop. Each page gets a new timeout, so a call without a caller deadline can continue indefinitely. An empty or unchanged cursor instead returns a partial model list as success. Track visited cursors and return an error when `has_more` is true but pagination cannot advance. Anthropic defines `has_more` as indicating further results and `last_id` as the next-page cursor. ([platform.claude.com](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/models/list?utm_source=openai))
